config.title: Zustand for Global State

intro.title: Zustand for Global State
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple counter app to learn how to manage global state across components using Zustand, a lightweight state management library for React. You'll understand the core concept of a global store—a single source of truth for state that can be accessed and updated from anywhere in your app without prop drilling. The main technologies involved are React functional components, Zustand's `create` function, and hooks like `useStore` to read and modify state. By the end, you'll be able to create a store, define state and actions, and connect multiple components to share and synchronize data seamlessly.
intro.usecase: Zustand is commonly used in modern React applications where multiple components need access to the same data without prop drilling. You'll see this in e-commerce sites where shopping cart state must be shared between product listings, cart previews, and checkout pages. Dashboard applications use Zustand to manage user preferences, theme settings, and filter states across various panels and widgets. It's also ideal for collaborative tools where real-time data like document editing status or user presence needs to be synchronized across different UI sections.

objectives: Initialize a Zustand store with state and actions.
Integrate the Zustand store into a React component.
Manipulate global state by invoking store actions from UI events.
Render dynamic content by binding component state to the Zustand store.
Configure a Zustand store to handle multiple state properties.
Apply Zustand to control shared state across multiple components.

steps.title: Import React and Zustand
steps.instruction: Import React and the create function from Zustand.
steps.hint: Use import statements at the top of the file. Zustand's create function is the default export from 'zustand'.
steps.seedCode: // Import React and Zustand's create function here
steps.expectedOutcome: The necessary libraries for React and Zustand are imported at the top of the file.
successCriteria: React is imported from 'react' and create is imported from 'zustand'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're importing both React and the create function from Zustand.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check your import statements. You need to import React from 'react' and create from 'zustand'.

steps.title: Create a Zustand store
steps.instruction: Define a Zustand store using the imported create function. Create a store named useStore with an initial state containing a count property set to 0 and an increment action.
steps.hint: Use const useStore = create((set) => ({ ... })) to define your store. Inside the object, include count: 0 and increment: () => set((state) => ({ count: state.count + 1 })).
steps.seedCode:
import { create } from 'zustand';

// Define your Zustand store here
steps.expectedOutcome: A Zustand store named useStore is created with initial state and an action.
successCriteria: The useStore is defined using create, includes count: 0 in the state, and has an increment action that updates count.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your store includes both the initial count state and the increment action that updates it.
steps.feedbackWrong: The store definition is missing or incorrect. Remember to use create, define count: 0, and include an increment action.

steps.title: Initialize store state
steps.instruction: Inside the store definition, add an initial state object with a property called 'count' set to 0.
steps.hint: The initial state should be an object with a count property initialized to 0.
steps.expectedOutcome: The store will have an initial state with count set to 0, ready to be used in components.
successCriteria: The store definition includes an initial state object with a count property set to 0.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added an object with a 'count' property set to 0 inside the store definition.
steps.feedbackWrong: The store definition doesn't yet have the required initial state. Add an object with a count property set to 0.

steps.title: Add store actions
steps.instruction: Inside the create callback, define an increment action that increases the count by 1 and a decrement action that decreases the count by 1. Use the set function to update the state.
steps.hint: Add two functions inside the object returned by create. Each function should call set with a state updater that modifies the count property.
steps.expectedOutcome: The store will have increment and decrement actions that can be called to modify the global count state.
successCriteria: The useStore has increment and decrement actions defined that use set to update the count.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure both increment and decrement actions are defined and use set to update count.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you've defined both increment and decrement actions inside the create callback using set.

steps.title: Create main component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named App that returns a div wrapper.
steps.hint: Define a function called App that returns JSX. Start with a simple div element.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have an App component that returns a div element, ready to contain your UI.
successCriteria: A functional component named App is defined and returns a div element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the main App component structure.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you have a function named App that returns a div element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The App component isn't defined correctly. Create a function named App that returns a div.

steps.title: Access store state in component
steps.instruction: Inside your App component, use the useStore hook to access the count state and store it in a variable.
steps.hint: Call the useStore hook and destructure the count property from the returned object.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: accessing state from a store
const count = useStore((state) => state.count);
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have access to the count value from the Zustand store.
successCriteria: The useStore hook is called and the count state is extracted into a variable.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're calling useStore and extracting the count property.
steps.feedbackWrong: Try again. You need to call the useStore hook and extract the count state from it.

steps.title: Access store actions in component
steps.instruction: Inside your App component, destructure the increment and decrement actions from the useStore hook.
steps.hint: The useStore hook returns an object containing both state and actions. Use destructuring to extract the increment and decrement functions.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: accessing actions from a store
const { increment, decrement } = useCounterStore();
steps.expectedOutcome: The increment and decrement actions are now available inside the App component for use in event handlers.
successCriteria: The increment and decrement actions are destructured from the useStore hook inside the App component.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're destructuring both increment and decrement actions from the useStore hook.
steps.feedbackWrong: The actions aren't properly accessed. Remember to call useStore() and destructure increment and decrement from the returned object.

steps.title: Add increment button
steps.instruction: Inside the App component's return statement, add a button element with the text 'Increment' that calls the increment action from the store when clicked.
steps.hint: Use the increment function you accessed from useStore in the onClick handler of the button.

successCriteria: The button element is added with the text 'Increment' and an onClick handler that calls the increment function.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.

steps.title: Export component
steps.instruction: Export the App component as the default export from this file.
steps.hint: Use the export default syntax to make the App component available for import in other files.

steps.expectedOutcome: The App component will be exported as the default export, making it ready to be imported and used in other parts of the application.
successCriteria: The App component is exported as default using export default App;
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're using the correct export syntax: export default App;
steps.feedbackWrong: The App component isn't properly exported. Use export default App; to make it available for import.
